summary: Balsalazide disodium is an aminosalicylate prodrug indicated for the treatment of mildly to moderately active ulcerative colitis in patients 5 years of age and older. It is delivered intact to the colon, where bacterial azoreduction releases mesalamine (5-aminosalicylic acid), the therapeutically active moiety, plus an inert carrier. The recommended adult dose is 2.25 g (three 750 mg capsules) three times daily for up to 8 weeks (some patients require up to 12 weeks). Capsules are swallowed whole, or may be opened and sprinkled on applesauce and swallowed immediately. Renal function should be assessed before and periodically during treatment. It is contraindicated in patients hypersensitive to salicylates or aminosalicylates. Important warnings include renal impairment, mesalamine-induced acute intolerance syndrome (which can mimic a colitis flare), hypersensitivity reactions including myocarditis and pericarditis, hepatic effects, and severe cutaneous adverse reactions.
indications: Treatment of mildly to moderately active ulcerative colitis in patients 5 years of age and older

moa: Balsalazide disodium is delivered intact to the colon, where it is cleaved by bacterial azoreduction to release equimolar amounts of mesalamine (5-aminosalicylic acid), the therapeutically active moiety, and an inert 4-aminobenzoyl-beta-alanine carrier that is only minimally absorbed. The mechanism of mesalamine is not fully understood but appears to be a local anti-inflammatory action on colonic epithelial cells. Mucosal production of arachidonic acid metabolites (prostanoids via cyclooxygenase, and leukotrienes and hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acids via lipoxygenase) is increased in ulcerative colitis, and mesalamine is thought to diminish inflammation by reducing the production of these mediators, with additional scavenging of reactive oxygen species.

absolute: Known or suspected hypersensitivity to salicylates, aminosalicylates, balsalazide metabolites, or any component of the product
relative: Known renal impairment or use of nephrotoxic drugs (assess and monitor renal function)
History of mesalamine-induced acute intolerance syndrome
Pyloric stenosis or other condition delaying gastric emptying
Pregnancy and lactation (use only if clearly needed)
monitor: Worsening colitis symptoms suggesting acute intolerance syndrome

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies of balsalazide in pregnant women. Mesalamine and its metabolites cross the placenta. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed; the potential benefit should justify any potential risk. Active maternal ulcerative colitis itself poses risks to pregnancy.
lact: Low concentrations of mesalamine and higher concentrations of its metabolite N-acetyl-5-ASA have been detected in human milk. Diarrhoea has been reported in breastfed infants exposed to oral 5-ASA products. Use with caution during breastfeeding and monitor the infant for diarrhoea; discontinue nursing or the drug if the infant is affected.
renal: Renal impairment, including interstitial nephritis and renal failure, has been reported with mesalamine products. Assess renal function before starting balsalazide and periodically during treatment. Weigh the risks and benefits in patients with known renal impairment or those taking nephrotoxic drugs, monitor renal function, and discontinue if renal function deteriorates.
hepatic: Hepatic failure has been reported in patients with pre-existing liver disease who were given other products containing mesalamine. Evaluate the risks and benefits of balsalazide in patients with known liver impairment.

major: Nephrotoxic agents including NSAIDs (additive renal toxicity - monitor renal function)
moderate: Azathioprine or 6-mercaptopurine (possible increased myelosuppression / blood dyscrasias)
Oral antibiotics (may alter colonic bacteria needed to activate the prodrug, potentially reducing efficacy)
minor: Other oral medicines - balsalazide may affect gut transit/absorption in some patients
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; adequate fluid intake advised
interactions.alcohol: No specific pharmacologic interaction with balsalazide
interactions.diagnostics: May cause increases in serum creatinine and liver enzymes; rare blood count changes

serious: Renal impairment, interstitial nephritis, renal failure
Mesalamine-induced acute intolerance syndrome (cramping, abdominal pain, bloody diarrhoea, fever - may mimic a flare)
Hypersensitivity reactions including myocarditis and pericarditis
Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (e.g. Stevens-Johnson syndrome, DRESS)

counsel: Take all three capsules three times a day exactly as prescribed, even when you feel better
Swallow the capsules whole; if you cannot, you may open them onto applesauce and swallow right away (this may temporarily stain teeth or tongue)
Drink plenty of fluids while taking this medicine
Tell your doctor if your colitis symptoms suddenly worsen (cramps, bloody diarrhoea, fever) - it could be an intolerance reaction
Report chest pain, shortness of breath, swelling, or markedly reduced urine output promptly
Mention any kidney problems or other medicines, especially anti-inflammatory painkillers (NSAIDs)
pk: Clinical improvement of colitis over days to weeks of regular dosing
Low and variable systemic absorption of intact balsalazide; mesalamine released in the colon
Highly variable systemic disposition; minimal systemic balsalazide exposure (acts locally in the colon)
Three-times-daily dosing maintains colonic mesalamine exposure; course of 8-12 weeks
Store at controlled room temperature (about 20-25 degrees C); protect from moisture
pearls: Colon-targeted 5-ASA prodrug - bacterial azoreduction releases mesalamine locally, sparing the small bowel and limiting systemic exposure.
Assess renal function before and during therapy; mesalamine-class drugs can cause interstitial nephritis and renal failure.
Mesalamine-induced acute intolerance syndrome can mimic a colitis flare (cramps, bloody diarrhoea, fever) - stop the drug if suspected.
Contraindicated in salicylate/aminosalicylate hypersensitivity; watch for rare myocarditis/pericarditis and severe skin reactions.
Capsules can be opened onto applesauce for patients who cannot swallow them, but transient teeth/tongue staining may occur.
Concomitant antibiotics may reduce efficacy by altering the colonic flora needed to activate the prodrug.
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular three-times-daily schedule - do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: As an aminosalicylate, balsalazide overdose may produce features of salicylate toxicity: nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, tachypnoea, hyperpnoea, tinnitus, and neurologic symptoms (headache, dizziness, confusion, seizures); severe intoxication can cause electrolyte and acid-base disturbances and organ (renal, hepatic) damage. There is no specific antidote. Manage with gastrointestinal decontamination (e.g. emesis, activated charcoal, cathartics) to limit absorption, correction of fluid and electrolyte imbalance, and supportive care.
